newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. sailor pleads guilty to Japan knife attack.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sailor pleads guilty to Japan knife attack.

text.p: A U.S. sailor pleaded guilty on Tuesday to charges of robbery and attempted murder in connection with a knife attack on a Japanese woman in July, a court spokesman said.

At a court hearing in the southwestern prefecture of Nagasaki, Seaman Terrence Michael Swanson, 20, admitted that he slashed the 20-year-old woman's throat and stole 13,000 yen ($118) from her handbag on July 16, said the spokesman for the Sasebo branch of Nagasaki District Court.
The incident took place near the U.S. Navy base in Sasebo, a port city 920 km (570 miles) south of Tokyo.
Swanson, from Anoka, Minnesota, had served on the guided missile frigate McClusky since November 1994. He was handed over to Japanese authorities after the incident.
Opposition to U.S. military bases in Japan heated up last year after three U.S. servicemen raped a 12-year-old schoolgirl on Japan's southwestern island of Okinawa.

The three were jailed earlier this year, but the high-profile case strained U.S.-Japan security ties and embroiled the Tokyo government in a tense legal and political battle with Okinawa over land occupied by U.S. bases.
